# `level_complex`

the navigation operators of one level of a surface's dyadic grid (d0, the Galerkin star1, the crossing map, d1 of the junctions), stored on the surface and keyed by the grid and the level.

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run level_complex --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run level_complex --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run select_dyadic_surface --dataset D --subject S --surface meg_surface --rule subject
nxr-neuro run level_complex --dataset D --subject S --surface meg_surface --tiles "meg_surface tiles" --spatial-scale "parts 16"
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `surface` | manifold surface, where {"name": "$surface"} (name the surface (--surface)) | yes |
| `tiles` | selection any, manifold surface.manifold.0, where {"name": "$tiles"} (the surface's dyadic grid (`nxr-neuro run select_dyadic_surface` first)) | yes |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `surface` | `--surface` | `required` | - |  | the surface whose grid's level is navigated, by name |
| `tiles` | `--tiles` | `required` | - |  | the surface's dyadic grid, by name |
| `spatial_scale` | `--spatial-scale` | `required` | - |  | the level as a quantity: parts per piece ("parts 16", a power of two), a tile diameter ("20 mm") or an area ("area 400 mm2"); the run records the level and the snapped quantity |
| `mesh` | `--mesh` | `operator` | - | operator, input | the fine complex the level coarsens: operator (the intrinsic Delaunay triangulation, whose Laplacian is every fine operator's) or input (the stored triangulation, whose 1-skeleton is the stored tile adjacency) |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`select.level_complex`](../nodes.md) | surface=surface, tiles=tiles | spatial_scale=$spatial_scale, mesh=$mesh | d0, star1, crossing, d1 |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `d0` | kind operator, operator_kind exterior derivative, name {tiles} L{level} d0, from surface.manifold.0, to surface.manifold.0, from_selection tiles |
| `star1` | kind operator, operator_kind hodge star, name {tiles} L{level} star1, from surface.manifold.0, to surface.manifold.0, from_selection tiles |
| `crossing` | kind operator, operator_kind crossing map, name {tiles} L{level} crossing, from surface.manifold.0, to surface.manifold.0, from_selection tiles |
| `d1` | kind operator, operator_kind exterior derivative, name {tiles} L{level} d1, from surface.manifold.0, to surface.manifold.0, from_selection tiles |

## Notes from the definition

```text
THE NAVIGATION OPERATORS OF ONE LEVEL OF A SURFACE'S DYADIC GRID (spec docs/specs/2026-11-26-levels-of-one-manifold.md): a level is no manifold of its own; it is the quotient of the
surface's fine complex by the grid's tiles at the level a stated scale sets, and its operators are stored ON THE SURFACE, keyed by (the surface, the grid, the level, the mesh, the metric):
  <grid> L<l> d0        its cells -> its edges (the pairs of tiles a fine edge joins, tail < tip, in pair order)
  <grid> L<l> star1     each edge's Galerkin conductance: the summed fine cotan weights across the boundary (the level's Laplacian d0' star1 d0 is the projected fine one)
  <grid> L<l> crossing  the surface's fine edges -> the level's edges (signed; d0_fine P = crossing d0)
  <grid> L<l> d1        its edges -> its junction faces (a fine face whose corners lie in three tiles)
star0 is the grid's own `w` (the tiles' barycentric areas). Whether the level makes a valid surface complex (halfedges with twin and next) and why not is in the producer record.
A consumer names it with `made_by: level_complex` (made once, when first needed). The time line's levels are closed form and store nothing.

THE GRAPH. surface (vertices, faces) + tiles (the grid at the stated level) --[select.level_complex]--> d0, star1, crossing, d1.

  nxr-neuro run select_dyadic_surface --dataset D --subject S --surface meg_surface --rule subject
  nxr-neuro run level_complex --dataset D --subject S --surface meg_surface --tiles "meg_surface tiles" --spatial-scale "parts 16"
```
